title: Domesday & Norman Control Adventure
welcome_lead: William has won — but how will he keep England? Castles, harshness and the famous Domesday Book. 📜
meta_desc: Norman Control Adventure — a KS3 walkthrough of how William the Conqueror controlled England after 1066.
final_note: You saw how castles, the Harrying of the North, feudalism and Domesday Book locked Norman power into England.

walkthroughs.body_html:
After 1066 the Normans were a small group ruling a hostile English population.

To control the country, William ordered motte-and-bailey castles built across England. They could go up in weeks using local peasant labour.

From these castles, Norman soldiers could quickly ride out and crush any local trouble. 🏰

In 1069 rebellion broke out in the north of England, helped by the Danes.

William's reply was terrible. In 1069–70, his soldiers burned villages, killed animals and destroyed food stores across Yorkshire.

This is called the Harrying of the North. Thousands died of starvation. It stopped any more rebellions for years.

William took land from Saxon lords and gave it to his Norman tenants-in-chief, who served him in return. This feudal system kept him in control.

In 1086 he sent officials all over England to record who owned what, how much it was worth, and how many people lived there.

The result was the Domesday Book — a giant survey, still used by historians today. 📚
